newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: INTERVIEW-S.Lanka DFCC sees bank mergers.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-S.Lanka DFCC sees bank mergers.

text.p: Sri Lanka is likely to see mergers and acquisitions in its banking and finance sector over the next few years, creating fewer but bigger bank groups, the DFCC Bank said on Wednesday.

DFCC chief executive Moksevi Prelis told Reuters in an interview the Indian Ocean island had a large number of relatively small financial institutions, many of which were too small to offer a full or very efficient service to their clients.
Sri Lanka has at more than 25 banks and a range of other smaller finance houses dealing with specialist lending.
"The proliferation of small financial institutions is not a healthy development because they are too small. They will have to amalgamate or merge to be good for this sector," he said.

DFCC, which earlier announced it had changed its name to reflect its new status as a specialist bank, is the largest financial group in Sri Lanka and the second largest company by capitalisation on the Colombo Stock Exchange.
Prelis said he could envisage a scenario in the future where DFCC Bank would tie up in some form with the state-owned Sri Lanka Insurance Corp and with Sri Lanka's Commercial Bank .
But he stressed there were no plans for such a grand alliance in the near future.
